newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Helix sees steps towards goldmining in '98.
newsitem.headline: Helix sees steps towards goldmining in '98.

text.p: Gold explorer Helix Resources NL said on Monday it hoped to see the first steps towards gold mine development on its promising Tunkillia prospect in South Australia's Gawler Craton region during calendar 1998.

At the company's annual meeting, chairman Ewen Tyler told shareholders he believed 1997 would see the definition of the scope of resources at Area 223 within the anomaly and elsewhere along its western demagnetised zone.

Tyler said the area covered by detailed drilling in Area 223, which had shown the potential to host a significant ore resource, represented less than three percent of the 25 square km area of gold in calcrete geochemical anomaly and the scope for further discoveries "must be rated highly".

Helix earlier on Monday released its March quarterly report, showing drilling results indicated gold mineralisatioon over at least 1,000 metres and potentially mineable mineralisation restricted to about 500m.

Helix said interpretation of drilling at Tunkillia indicated the 500 metre zone contained a series of narrow high grade zones ranging from 5.4 grams per tonne (g/t) gold, to 25.5 g/t over drilled intervals of one to 14 metres.
At 0450 GMT (2.50 p.m.), Helix shares were down 20 cents at A$1.80, a level only 15 cents above its 12-month low, and well below its high of A$4.99. Volume was 108,722 shares.
